title: Cranberry Whipped Cream
description: Tart cranberry purée whipped into lightly sweet cream: blush pink, holiday-bright, and sturdy enough to make ahead.

items.note: about 6 oz; no need to thaw

steps.text: Combine {cranberries}, {sugar}, {juice}, and a pinch of salt in a small saucepan over medium heat. Simmer, stirring and pressing the berries against the pan, until they've all burst and the mixture is thick and jammy, 8 to 10 minutes.
steps.why: Cooking it down to jam is about driving off water. Every bit of liquid left in the purée is liquid the cream has to carry, and a thin purée deflates whipped cream.

steps.text: Push the hot mixture through a fine-mesh sieve with a spatula, scraping the underside into a bowl. Discard the skins and seeds. You want a thick, glossy purée about the consistency of ketchup.
steps.why: Skins and seeds leave flecks and grit in something that should be silky. If the purée looks loose, return it to the pan and reduce a few more minutes.

steps.text: Chill the purée completely, at least 1 hour in the fridge, or spread it thin on a plate and freeze 15 minutes.
steps.why: Warm purée melts the fat in cold cream, and melted fat won't hold air. It must be fully cold before it meets the cream.

steps.text: Chill the mixing bowl and beaters or whisk in the freezer for 10 minutes before whipping.
steps.why: Cold equipment keeps the cream's fat firm, which is what traps the air. A warm bowl means slower whipping and a softer result.

steps.text: Whip {cream}, {powdered-sugar}, and {vanilla} to soft peaks: the cream holds a shape that slumps over at the tip.
steps.why: Powdered sugar contains cornstarch, which helps stabilize the cream so it holds longer once the acidic purée goes in.

steps.text: Add the cold cranberry purée and whip just until medium peaks form and the color is even blush pink. Stop the moment the tips stand up and curl slightly.
steps.why: Cranberry's acid tightens cream fast, so it goes from soft to stiff in seconds. Overwhipped cream turns grainy and starts heading toward butter.

steps.text: Serve right away, or cover and refrigerate. Give it a few gentle strokes with a whisk before serving if it has loosened.

notes.title: Make-ahead
notes.body: The purée keeps 5 days refrigerated, so make it ahead and whip the cream the day you serve. The finished whipped cream holds 1 to 2 days covered in the fridge.

notes.title: No sieve?
notes.body: Let the cooked cranberries cool to warm, then blend smooth in a blender. Never blend them hot in a sealed blender: steam pressure can blow the lid. Blended purée keeps a little more texture than sieved.

notes.title: If it goes grainy
notes.body: Overwhipped cream can be rescued: gently whisk in a splash of cold heavy cream by hand until it smooths out again.

plating: A generous spoonful on each slice, swooped with the back of the spoon so the pink catches the light. A few sugared cranberries or a pinch of orange zest on top if you want a finish.
elevations: Finely grated orange zest whipped in with the purée: cranberry and orange are a natural pair.
A tablespoon of Grand Marnier or another orange liqueur with the vanilla.
A spoonful of freeze-dried cranberry powder for deeper color and flavor without adding any liquid.
